title: Medical-Surgical Nursing Progress Note
brief: A medical-surgical nursing progress note for a hospitalized patient, drafted from the shift assessment and medication record.

slip.document:
# Medical-Surgical Nursing Progress Note
Juniper Valley Medical Center | 04/18/2026 | 0700–1500 shift

## Patient and baseline
Patient: Rosa Osei, 58, room 214; attending: Dr. Brandon Banerjee. Alert and oriented ×4; full code. Megan Maddox, RN, received report at 0700.

| Item | 0700 assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Temperature | 98.6 °F oral |
| Blood pressure | 132/78 mmHg |
| Heart rate | 84 beats/min |
| Respiratory rate | 16 breaths/min |
| SpO₂ | 97% on room air |
| Pain | 7/10, right lower abdomen |
| Allergies | Penicillin: hives |

## Shift note
At 0715, patient reported right lower abdominal pain, 7/10, worse with movement. Abdomen soft, mildly tender at the surgical site; dressing clean, dry, and intact. Bowel sounds present in all four quadrants. No nausea or vomiting reported. Peripheral IV in left forearm patent without redness or swelling.

At 0730, oxycodone 5 mg by mouth administered for pain per active order and MAR. No known allergies reported. Patient took medication with water and remained in bed with call light within reach. At 0800, patient was awake and conversing with her daughter; vital signs were stable as documented above.

At 1030, patient ambulated 120 ft in the hallway with a gait belt and one-person standby assist. Denied dizziness or shortness of breath. At 1200, ate approximately 75% of lunch and tolerated fluids. Voided 350 mL clear yellow urine. Surgical dressing remained clean, dry, and intact on reassessment.

## Handoff
At 1500, patient resting in bed, call light within reach. Report given to receiving RN, including mobility tolerance, intake and output, and current pain complaint. Continue ordered assessments and medication plan; notify the provider for new or worsening symptoms.

errors.quote: At 0730, oxycodone 5 mg by mouth administered for pain per active order and MAR.
errors.explanation: After administering an opioid for pain, the chart should include follow-up assessment of pain and relevant safety findings, such as sedation and respiratory status. No such reassessment is documented after the 0730 dose.
errors.fix: At 0800, pain was reassessed and sedation and respiratory status were assessed and documented.

errors.explanation: The allergy table lists penicillin causing hives, so documenting no known allergies contradicts the recorded allergy and could lead to unsafe medication administration.
